summary: A stand-alone demo script that builds three simple five-year financial models from typed-in numbers and prints the tables.
purpose: Show how a simple three-statement model works without the web app or the database.
why: Likely reason: a learning or demo file. The printed next steps suggest it is meant to be edited.
how: Sets up the imports and printed headers. A class calculates revenue, costs, operating profit, depreciation, taxes, net income and free cash flow for each year, and returns two tables. Three example companies run through it, then a summary is printed.
inputs: Numbers typed into the code: starting revenue, growth rates, cost shares, capital spending and tax rate.
outputs: Printed tables and summary lines in the console. No file is saved.
risks: It is simplified: no working capital changes, no credit for tax losses, and depreciation starts in the year of purchase. Lists are matched by position, and if their lengths differ, values are dropped silently.
debug: If numbers look wrong, check that each percent and growth list has one entry per year. Run it from a terminal to see the printed output.
